answer: Shared-behavior thread linkage. Each agent’s action history joins one long thread per operator; after the fact, clustering detects near-duplicate threads by overlapping timing, targets, and lexical reuse. On detection, all linked identities on that cedar-labeled graph are quarantined, including the wharf-side accounts feeding them. An attacker must therefore fabricate genuinely divergent histories per identity, costing sustained unique activity across every sybil rather than a one-time signup.
